quests.instruction: You are visiting your grandparents' home and do not know where anything is. Which is the safest way to explore?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask before opening doors or touching things 🗣️
options: Open every door to find what you need 🚪
Wait quietly until someone notices you ⏳
Ask before opening doors or touching things 🗣️
quests.hint: A home you do not know has surprises, such as stairs, tools, or pets.
quests.explanation: Asking first keeps you safe in a place where you do not know the layout or the rules. Opening every door could lead to a cupboard with chemicals or a steep staircase.
quests.funFact: Each home has its own rules, even among families who are close.

quests.instruction: Grandma's staircase is steep and has no light switch at the bottom. Which plan keeps you safest?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask for the light and hold the rail 💡
options: Ask for the light and hold the rail 💡
Go down fast before it gets darker 🏃
Use your phone screen and no rail 📱
quests.hint: Combine seeing the steps with a steady hold.
quests.explanation: Light and a handrail work together, since light shows the steps and the rail keeps you balanced. Hurrying or using a phone only makes a fall more likely.
quests.funFact: Older homes often have steeper stairs than newer ones.

quests.instruction: Grandpa's old kettle has no automatic switch-off and is boiling. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Stay back, let a grown-up handle it ♨️
options: Lift it to help pour for everyone at once 🫖
Switch it off and carry it away fast 🔌
Stay back, let a grown-up handle it ♨️
quests.hint: A different home may have older appliances you do not know how to use.
quests.explanation: Boiling water and unfamiliar equipment are for adults. Staying back keeps you safe from steam and spills.
quests.funFact: Older kettles can keep boiling or get hot on the outside, unlike many newer ones.

quests.instruction: A family has just arrived at a new home with a truck full of boxes. Which box should be opened first?
quests.correctAnswer: The box of toothbrushes, towels, and bedding 📦
options: The box of picture frames and decorations 🖼️
The box of toothbrushes, towels, and bedding 📦
The box of out-of-season clothes 🧥
quests.hint: Think about what you will need before the end of the first day.
quests.explanation: Basics like toothbrushes, towels, and bedding are needed straight away. Decorations and off-season clothes can wait.
quests.funFact: An 'open first' box with the basics makes the first night in a new home easier.

quests.instruction: How can labels make unpacking faster after a move?
quests.correctAnswer: Write the room and contents on each box 🏷️
options: Write the room and contents on each box 🏷️
Put no labels so it feels like a surprise 🎁
Write only the family name on every box ✏️
quests.hint: A box with a clear label can go straight to the right place.
quests.explanation: A label with the room and contents lets helpers take each box to the correct spot. Boxes without labels have to be opened to find out.
quests.funFact: Colored stickers for each room make labels easy to read quickly.

quests.instruction: In a new home, which safety check should come first?
quests.correctAnswer: Smoke alarms and clear exits 🚨
options: Smoke alarms and clear exits 🚨
Which wall color looks best 🎨
Where to hang the family photos 🖼️
quests.hint: A new home is unfamiliar, so safety comes before looks.
quests.explanation: Alarms and exits protect everyone, so grown-ups check them on day one. Paint colors and photo places come later.
quests.funFact: Planning an escape route and a meeting spot is a good first job in a new home.

quests.instruction: A family lives in a small one-room flat where the cooking corner is near the bed. What helps keep things safe and tidy?
quests.correctAnswer: Keep the bed area clear of spills 🛏️
options: Move the stove next to the pillows 🔥
Keep the bed area clear of spills 🛏️
Leave tools on the bed to save space 🍳
quests.hint: Different jobs in one room need clear zones.
quests.explanation: Keeping sleeping and cooking spaces apart prevents burns and mess. In a small room, using zones is more important than ever.
quests.funFact: Folding screens or curtains can divide a single room into zones.

quests.instruction: There is no hallway: the front door opens straight into the main room. What keeps shoes and mud under control?
quests.correctAnswer: A mat and a shoe basket 👟
options: A mat and a shoe basket 👟
Nothing, mud will not matter 🤷
Shoes stored beside the bed 🛏️
quests.hint: Put the solution where the problem begins.
quests.explanation: A mat and a basket by the door catch mud and give shoes a home right at the entrance. Shoes by the bed bring dirt into the sleeping area.
quests.funFact: Even in the smallest flats, a small spot by the door can be an entry area.

quests.instruction: A home has no garden. Where could children play ball safely?
quests.correctAnswer: A nearby park, with a grown-up 🌳
options: In the living room with vases 🛋️
A nearby park, with a grown-up 🌳
On a balcony with a low rail 🏙️
quests.hint: Space and safety both matter.
quests.explanation: A park gives room to run and has no breakable items. Indoors things could break, and balconies can be dangerous for ball games.
quests.funFact: Many towns have parks and playgrounds so children without gardens can play.

quests.instruction: A family is planning dinner for six guests. Which task should come first?
quests.correctAnswer: Decide the menu and check needs 📋
options: Choose the evening music 🎵
Pick the napkins for the table 🍽️
Decide the menu and check needs 📋
quests.hint: Everything else depends on what will be eaten.
quests.explanation: The menu shapes the shopping, cooking, and setting up, and asking about food needs keeps guests safe. Music and napkins can be decided later.
quests.funFact: Asking guests about foods they cannot eat is a polite habit.

quests.instruction: Which timeline works best for hosting a dinner?
quests.correctAnswer: Prepare, cook, set table, serve, clean up 🍳
options: Serve, set the table, cook, prepare, clean 🍽️
Prepare, cook, set table, serve, clean up 🍳
Clean up, serve, cook, set the table 🧽
quests.hint: Everything must be ready before it is served.
quests.explanation: Food is prepared and cooked before it is served, and the table is set in time. Cleaning up comes after the meal.
quests.funFact: Cooks often write a short timeline so that nothing is forgotten.

quests.instruction: Which job plan for the dinner is safest and fairest?
quests.correctAnswer: Child sets table, adult cooks 🍽️
options: Child sets table, adult cooks 🍽️
Child cooks on the stove, adult sets the table 🍳
Child carries hot pots, adult greets guests 🍲
quests.hint: Decide who should do which kind of job.
quests.explanation: A child setting the table is safe and helpful. The stove, knives, and hot pots are for adults.
quests.funFact: A job list on the fridge helps every helper know what to do.

quests.instruction: On a family home-safety walk-through, which is the best thing to check first?
quests.correctAnswer: Alarms work and exits are clear 🚪
options: Whether shelves are dusted 🧹
Whether paint is still fresh 🎨
Alarms work and exits are clear 🚪
quests.hint: Ask yourself what protects people in an emergency.
quests.explanation: Working alarms and clear exits are the most important safety features. Dusting and paint matter far less.
quests.funFact: Many fire services suggest testing alarms regularly, such as once a month.

quests.instruction: A walk-through spots a beeping smoke alarm, a dusty shelf, and some faded paint. Which should be reported first?
quests.correctAnswer: The beeping smoke alarm 🚨
options: The dusty shelf 🌫️
The beeping smoke alarm 🚨
The faded paint 🎨
quests.hint: One of the three affects safety.
quests.explanation: A beeping smoke alarm may need a new battery, so a grown-up should deal with it quickly. Dust and faded paint are not urgent.
quests.funFact: A chirping alarm is asking for a fix, not a sign of a fire.

quests.instruction: After a safety walk-through, what is the best way to use what was found?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a grown-up and make a fix list 📋
options: Keep it secret to avoid worrying anyone 🤫
Try to fix everything yourself 🔧
Tell a grown-up and make a fix list 📋
quests.hint: Noticing is the first part, and action needs the right people.
quests.explanation: A list helps the family decide what to fix and who can do it. Children report what they see, and adults take care of repairs.
quests.funFact: A checklist with ticks makes progress easy to see.

quests.instruction: Two families tidy differently: one does everything on Sunday, the other tidies a little every evening. Which works better over time?
quests.correctAnswer: A short tidy every evening ⏱️
options: A short tidy every evening ⏱️
One huge session every Sunday 📅
Waiting until nobody can find anything 🔍
quests.hint: Small jobs done often stay small.
quests.explanation: Daily short tidying keeps the mess from building up. Big sessions can feel overwhelming, and waiting makes the job harder.
quests.funFact: A song or a timer can make a ten-minute tidy feel quick.

quests.instruction: Two storage plans: bins that are sorted and named, or a closed pile in a corner. Which is better?
quests.correctAnswer: Sorted, named bins within reach 📦
options: A closed pile in the corner 🧱
Sorted, named bins within reach 📦
One big box with everything inside 🗃️
quests.hint: A plan should help you find and return things easily.
quests.explanation: Labeled bins at a reachable height let anyone see where things go. A pile or one huge box makes things hard to find.
quests.funFact: Bins at a child's height are easier for small hands to use and to put back.

quests.instruction: After a muddy afternoon, one family wipes shoes at the door and the other walks straight in. Which approach is better, and why?
quests.correctAnswer: Wiping at the door, so mud stays outside 🚪
options: Wiping at the door, so mud stays outside 🚪
Walking in, because mops fix everything 🪣
Walking in, since the floors will dry anyway 💧
quests.hint: Stopping mess at the source saves cleaning later.
quests.explanation: Dealing with mud at the door keeps it from spreading through the home. Cleaning afterward takes much longer.
quests.funFact: A good mat can trap most of the dirt that shoes carry.

quests.instruction: A child is helping make fruit salad with a grown-up. Which order is the best and safest?
quests.correctAnswer: Wash hands and fruit, adult cuts, mix, clean 🍓
options: Mix, cut with a big knife, wash fruit, eat 🔪
Eat, wash hands, cut, mix, clean up 🍽️
Wash hands and fruit, adult cuts, mix, clean 🍓
quests.hint: Hygiene first, sharp tools by an adult, cleanup last.
quests.explanation: Hands and fruit are washed first, an adult handles the cutting, then mixing, serving, and cleaning follow. The other orders skip hygiene or give a child the sharp tool.
quests.funFact: Fruit that is cut and left out too long can spoil, so salads are best made fresh.

quests.instruction: Some fruit salad is left. What is the best way to store it?
quests.correctAnswer: In a covered box in the fridge 🧊
options: In an open bowl on the counter 🍽️
In a covered box in the fridge 🧊
In a sealed bag on a sunny shelf ☀️
quests.hint: Cut fruit needs cold and cover.
quests.explanation: Cold slows spoilage, and a cover keeps out dust and smells. The warm counter or sunny shelf lets germs grow.
quests.funFact: Cut fruit is best eaten within a day or two.

quests.instruction: Which kitchen item in this job needs a grown-up, not a child?
quests.correctAnswer: The sharp knife 🔪
options: The mixing spoon 🥄
The sharp knife 🔪
The empty bowl 🥣
quests.hint: Consider what could cut.
quests.explanation: A sharp knife can cause serious cuts, so adults use it. A spoon and a bowl are safe for a child to handle.
quests.funFact: Child-safe knives exist for soft foods like bananas.

quests.instruction: You find a warm, humming device you do not recognize plugged in under the sofa. What is the best choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Stay away and tell a grown-up 🔌
options: Unplug it with your wet hands 💧
Open it up to see what it is 🔩
Stay away and tell a grown-up 🔌
quests.hint: Unfamiliar electrical things deserve extra caution.
quests.explanation: A warm, humming device might be overheating, so a grown-up should check it. Wet hands and opening it up can cause a shock.
quests.funFact: Some devices stay warm normally, but an adult can tell what is expected.

quests.instruction: A sweet chemical smell is coming from a closed cupboard. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Do not open it, tell a grown-up 🧪
options: Open it to find the source 🗄️
Light a candle to hide it 🕯️
Do not open it, tell a grown-up 🧪
quests.hint: A smell without a known cause can be a warning.
quests.explanation: Strange smells can come from chemicals or leaks. Leave the cupboard shut and tell an adult, and never light flames near an unknown smell.
quests.funFact: Opening a window gives fresh air while the adult checks.

quests.instruction: A neighbor drops by with a parcel for your parents, and a grown-up is nearby. What is best?
quests.correctAnswer: Call the grown-up to the door 📞
options: Call the grown-up to the door 📞
Open the door and take it yourself 🚪
Ignore the doorbell 🔔
quests.hint: A grown-up is close, so use them.
quests.explanation: Calling the adult over keeps you safe and lets them thank the neighbor. Ignoring the bell is not polite, and handling it alone is not needed.
quests.funFact: Neighbors often help each other with deliveries and small favors.

quests.instruction: A baby cousin is coming to visit. Which change makes the home safer for her?
quests.correctAnswer: Put small items and cleaners away 🧴
options: Leave everything where it is 🙈
Put small items and cleaners away 🧴
Put everything on the floor 🧸
quests.hint: Remember how babies explore: by grabbing and tasting.
quests.explanation: Small items and cleaners can be swallowed or cause harm, so they go high up or away. Leaving them at floor level is risky.
quests.funFact: A tip for grown-ups is to get down on hands and knees to see what a baby can reach.

quests.instruction: Which toys are best to put out for the baby?
quests.correctAnswer: Large soft toys, no small parts 🧸
options: Bricks with tiny pieces 🧱
A box of marbles and buttons 🔵
Large soft toys, no small parts 🧸
quests.hint: Think about what can fit into a small mouth.
quests.explanation: Large soft toys are safe and easy to hold. Marbles, buttons, and small bricks can be swallowed.
quests.funFact: Toy packaging often shows a small warning symbol for children under three.

quests.instruction: A baby gate is available. Where is it most useful in a home?
quests.correctAnswer: At the top of the stairs 🚧
options: At the top of the stairs 🚧
In the middle of the garden 🌳
Beside the sofa 🛋️
quests.hint: Think about a fall that could cause serious harm.
quests.explanation: A gate at the top of the stairs keeps a crawling baby from falling. It needs to be fixed securely by an adult.
quests.funFact: Gates can also block kitchens, so babies stay away from hot things.

quests.instruction: After a week away, your family opens the front door to a dark, stuffy home. Which order is the best way to settle in?
quests.correctAnswer: Lights on, bags down, wash hands, unpack 🧳
options: Lights on, bags down, wash hands, unpack 🧳
Unpack the fridge, lights on, bags by the door, wash hands 🧊
Wash hands, unpack the fridge, bags by the door, lights on 🧼
quests.hint: You need to see before you can do anything else.
quests.explanation: Lights come first so everyone can see and move safely, then bags are put out of the way, hands get washed, and food is dealt with. The other orders put food or washing ahead of light and safety.
quests.funFact: Checking that everything looks normal on arrival is part of coming home.

quests.instruction: It is a hot day and the power cuts out. Food is in the fridge. Which choice shows the best judgment?
quests.correctAnswer: Keep doors closed, let a grown-up decide 🧊
options: Open the fridge every ten minutes to check 👀
Keep doors closed, let a grown-up decide 🧊
Eat everything quickly before it spoils 🍽️
quests.hint: Cold stays in only when the door stays shut.
quests.explanation: A closed fridge keeps its cold for hours. A grown-up can check the food afterward and decide what is safe to eat.
quests.funFact: Thermometers inside fridges help adults know whether food stayed cold enough.

quests.instruction: Which sentence best sums up what you have learned about homes?
quests.correctAnswer: A home works when people care and ask when unsure 🏠
options: A home works when each person looks after only their own room 🛏️
A home works when everything is done without anyone's help 🦸
A home works when people care and ask when unsure 🏠
quests.hint: Think about everything from rooms to routines to safety.
quests.explanation: Homes are shared places. They work best when people look after the space and each other, and ask for help when they are not sure.
quests.funFact: No two homes are exactly alike, yet the same habits help every one of them.
